# Netsertive's MLX 3\.0 introduces AI-driven central command platform for franchise marketing

Netsertive launches MLX 3\.0, a new iteration of its multi-location platform featuring AI-native tools to streamline reporting, optimise campaigns, and enhance visibility for franchise groups managing extensive local\.\.\.

Netsertive launches MLX 3\.0, a new iteration of its multi-location platform featuring AI-native tools to streamline reporting, optimise campaigns, and enhance visibility for franchise groups managing extensive local networks\.

Netsertive has unveiled the latest iteration of its Multi-Location Experience platform, positioning the software as a central command hub for franchise groups and other brands that manage dozens or hundreds of local presences\. According to the company’s announcement, MLX 3\.0 is designed to move customers away from fragmented reporting and towards a more active operating model, in which campaign data, local performance and execution tools sit in one place\.

The company says the new version is built around an AI-native layer that sits on top of consolidated local data, with the aim of reducing the time marketers spend stitching together information from spreadsheets, customer relationship systems and separate advertising tools\. Netsertive says the platform now combines analytics, campaign management and recommendations in a way that should make it easier for brand teams and local operators to monitor results, understand revenue impact and react more quickly to changing conditions\.

Among the features highlighted are AI-powered tools including a chat assistant, AI-search optimisation and call-analysis functions, which the company says can surface trends, suggest improvements and generate narrative guidance for users\. Herb Brittner, Netsertive’s vice-president of product and engineering, said the shift is intended to replace lagging dashboards with more actionable insight\. The company also says the platform draws on several model and cloud components, including Amazon Bedrock and Nova Micro, Snowflake Cortex and Google Gemini, depending on the task\.

Netsertive says MLX 3\.0 also adds practical controls for distributed marketing teams, including a web content editor for updating location pages centrally, plus an active location directory and interactive map intended to improve visibility across networks\. The company’s wider platform already supports coordinated national and local activity across search, social, display, video, connected TV, reviews, listings and location pages, and Netsertive says the latest release continues a broader push to unify those functions while preserving local customisation\.

Netsertive specializes in localized digital marketing technology solutions and counts, among its 100\+ multi-location customers, growing brands including Mosquito Shield, Re-Bath, DreamMaker Bath and Kitchen, America's Mattress, and Pet Supplies Plus\. To determine the Top Franchise Suppliers, *Entrepreneur* surveyed more than 900 franchisors to find out which service providers they and their local franchisees use, and to rate their satisfaction with the quality, cost, and value of the services\. They scored each supplier based on the survey results, and the top-scoring suppliers in marketing and technology services, as well as 10 other business categories, were list-ranked\. \"*Entrepreneu*r's Top Franchise Suppliers list underscores some of the aspects of the industry that are easy to miss, but critical to a franchise's success,\" said *Entrepreneur *Senior Vice President of Franchising Liane Caruso\. \"The 134 companies ranked in this year's list help to handle critical aspects of business by providing vital services to franchisors and franchisees, such as accounting, financing, legal services, marketing, real estate assistance, and more\.\"

**RESEARCH TRIANGLE REGION, N\.C\. –**Netsertive, a marketing technology company empowering brands, national retailers and local businesses to automate and scale distributed local marketing, announced today the acquisition of Mixpo, a Seattle-based creative management platform that enables publishers and marketers to easily build, manage and measure compelling video and rich media ad campaigns\. Together, the companies will offer a next-generation platform that solves the complexity, speed and workflow challenges in executing full-funnel digital marketing campaigns at the local level\.

“Brands and their distributed retail networks must adapt to the complex reality of a click-to-brick economy,” said Brendan Morrissey, CEO and co-founder of Netsertive\. “With the combined capabilities of Netsertive and Mixpo, our clients can scale their digital marketing across local retailer networks of any size to reach digital shoppers, influence their choice of products, and ultimately drive buyers to local businesses\. We’ve thoroughly enjoyed working with the Mixpo team as a partner for the past year\. The success we’ve had working together led us down the path of coming together as a single company\.”

Netsertive’s acquisition of Mixpo strengthens its position as the fastest-growing brand-to-local marketing tech platform at a critical time for brick-and-mortar retail\. Today, more than 90 percent of retail sales are transacted in-store, but the Internet now dominates the critical first engagements that influence what and where people buy\. Still, many brands are not including local stores in their omnichannel marketing strategies, resulting in missed opportunities to help buyers complete their path to purchase locally\.

“Mixpo’s interactive ad formats and dynamic localization capabilities are perfectly aligned with Netsertive’s broader brand-to-local marketing technology,” said Charlie Tillinghast, CEO of Mixpo\. “Our joint offering will deliver tremendous value to brands and publishers looking to accelerate both the delivery and impact of their omnichannel marketing\.”

Collectively, Netsertive and Mixpo service hundreds of enterprise brands and thousands of local locations\. The combined client base includes many of the world’s top publishers as well as dozens of the most recognized brands and agencies\. By integrating Mixpo’s creative workflow solution with Netsertive’s brand-to-local marketing technology platform, brands and resellers will be able to access a full-stack marketing solution that will scale across the most critical media channels in reaching local buyers: search, social, video, mobile, rich media and display\. The combined offering will afford brands and campaign managers insights into performance on these channels and the ability to modify campaigns in real time, while enabling advertisers with access to the premium local advertising inventory of Mixpo’s publisher partners\.

This deal continues a cycle of growth and momentum for Netsertive\. At the end of 2016, Netsertive reported 400 percent revenue growth over the past three years and expanded its workforce to more than 250 team members\. The company also signed several new major brand clients in 2016, and reported continued success with top brands such as Serta, Whirlpool, Electrolux, FCA, Acura and more\.

Netsertive has revolutionized how brands and local businesses work together to win local customers\. The company’s two complementary solutions, MarketWise™ for Brands and StreetWise™ for Local Businesses, enable cooperative marketing by giving brands the capability to activate scaled omnichannel marketing campaigns\. The innovative technology combines the company’s deep industry experience with the collective intelligence of its extensive network of automotive, home goods, technology and healthcare clients to deliver unprecedented campaign speed, performance and value\. An award-winning marketing technology company and Google Premier and Bing Elite SMB Partner, Netsertive helps enterprise brands automate their co-op marketing to ensure localized brand compliance, campaign execution and reimbursement tracking for distributed local partners\.

Founded in 2009 and based in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, the company has a history of rapid growth, a world-class team and the strength of venture capital funding from top firms RRE Ventures, Harbert Venture Partners, River Cities Capital Funds and Greycroft Partners\. # Starsand Island Worldwide Release Date Announced - Newsy Today

Starsand Island will launch its full version on August 18, 2026, according to developer Seed Sparkle Lab, following an extended Early Access period\. Global release times are set for 05:00 PDT, 08:00 EDT, 13:00 BST, 20:00 SGT, and 21:00 JST, bringing a comprehensive suite of pastoral simulation updates and new relationship systems to the island life game\.

The August 18, 2026 launch date marks the end of the game’s Early Access phase\. Seed Sparkle Lab confirms that the full version introduces massive content updates, including non-player character updates, dedicated relationship quests, additional dating activities, and upcoming seasonal events\.

## Living Island World and Gameplay Systems

According to Seed Sparkle Lab, Starsand Island operates on a dynamic four-season cycle that directly shapes daily life, farming routines, exploration conditions, and community activities\. The pastoral simulation combines farming, crafting, ranching, fishing, and production systems\. These mechanics evolve alongside the player, becoming more streamlined over time to give users greater freedom to explore and pace their island life\.

## Exploration and Community Mechanics

Beyond the pastoral idyll, players can explore ancient ruins, mine valuable resources, and encounter fantastical creatures in locations like the Moonlit Forest\. Social interaction forms a core pillar of the experience\. Residents feature distinct personalities and professions, allowing players to build long-term bonds, unlock personal storylines, and experience emotional moments through everyday engagement\.

## Customization and Lifestyle Features

Seed Sparkle Lab has built robust customization options into Starsand Island, spanning player character appearance, home building, and interior decoration\. Seasonal festivals, cooking mechanics, and a varied fashion system further enhance the cultural flavor of the coastal setting\. Players can spend their days interacting with capybaras, cats, and dogs, or engage in bountiful fishing excursions away from the urban grind\.

# Xiaomi MIX Fold 5 Just Appeared in Live Photos Running HyperOS 4

This is real hardware, real software, and a real leak\. The \"lhasa\" codename is visible, its OS version starts with 4\.0 and Android 17 is confirmed\.

#### Summary

- Live photos circulating online show an active foldable device displaying the \"lhasa\" codename in its software information page — the internal designation Xiaomi has used for the MIX Fold 5 across multiple certification filings since mid-2026\.
- The software version string visible in the images begins with 4\.0, making this the first real-world photographic confirmation of Xiaomi HyperOS 4 running on a physical device\.
- Android 17is shown as the base OS version, confirming HyperOS 4 will ship on the Android 17 platform — a detail that aligns with Xiaomi's previous pattern of pairing each major HyperOS generation with the corresponding Android release\.
- The MIX Fold 5 is expected to be the launch device for HyperOS 4, with AI-powered system applications and deeper cross-device integration as its headline software features\.
- The physical hardware visible in the photos matches Xiaomi's expected book-style foldable design for the MIX Fold 5 — an August 2026 China launch remains the most credible timeline based on the device's 2608 model number date code\.

> A codename visible on a live device's software information screen is about as close to confirmation as you get before an official announcement\. 'Lhasa' running HyperOS 4\.0 on Android 17 is not a render, not a spec sheet, and not a Geekbench entry — it's a working phone, in someone's hands, today\.

#### What the Photos Actually Confirm

Two images are circulating\. The first shows a book-style foldable device with its outer display active, showing a lock screen interface consistent with Xiaomi's current design language — updated with elements that differ visually from HyperOS 3\. The second shows the device's software information page in Chinese, where the \"lhasa\" codename and the version string beginning with \"4\.0\" are reportedly visible alongside Android 17 as the base platform\.

The \"lhasa\" codename has appeared consistently in MIX Fold 5 documentation across IMEI filings, internal ROM entries, and supply chain reports throughout 2026\. Its appearance on a live device in active use eliminates the possibility of this being a rendered mock-up or early prototype not representative of the final product\.

#### HyperOS 4: What We Know So Far

HyperOS 4 on Android 17 represents Xiaomi's first major OS generation tied to the new Android 17 platform — the same base used by Samsung's One UI 9 and OnePlus's OxygenOS 16\. For Xiaomi, the upgrade from HyperOS 3 to HyperOS 4 is expected to center on three areas: deeper AI model integration at the system level, expanded cross-device workflows between phones, tablets, cars, and smart home products, and a visual refresh toward the translucent glass-influenced design direction that Android 17 introduces across the broader ecosystem\.

The MIX Fold 5 launching with HyperOS 4 pre-installed means Xiaomi's foldable flagship will be the first device globally to ship this software to consumers — a meaningful marketing position heading into an August launch window\.

#### August Launch and What Comes Next

The 2608 date code in the MIX Fold 5's model numbers points to August 2026\. Xiaomi Day falls on August 8 — an annual company event Xiaomi has used to launch flagship hardware\. The live photo appearance in the third week of July is consistent timing for pre-launch hardware testing reaching the stage where devices move outside controlled environments\. Expect official teaser activity to begin in the coming days\.

# GameStop’s Zelda Ocarina of Time Pre-Order “Leak” Looks Like an Error

Share this article

Nintendo has confirmed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 in 2026, but it has not announced an official release date or pre-order schedule\. \(Nintendo\)

**Nintendo** officially announced **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** for **Switch 2** in June, but it has not yet revealed the game’s release date, price, or pre-order schedule\. That lack of information recently turned what appears to be a retailer error into a widely shared Zelda “leak\.”

A GameStop search result reportedly displayed an August 4, 2026 date alongside the upcoming Ocarina of Time release\. Some fans interpreted the date as the start of pre-orders or even a possible launch date\.

However, the available evidence suggests that the date probably did not belong to Zelda at all\.

## The August 4 Date Likely Came From Another Game

August 4, 2026 is the confirmed release date for Beast of Reincarnation, an upcoming action RPG from Game Freak\. GameStop already has active product pages and pre-order information for the game\.

This makes a retailer database or search indexing error the most plausible explanation\. GameStop or Google may have pulled the August 4 date from Beast of Reincarnation and temporarily attached it to the Ocarina of Time search result\.

GameStop subsequently removed the date, and Nintendo has not made any related announcement\.

The incident therefore should not be treated as confirmation that Ocarina of Time pre-orders will begin on August 4\. It also does not reliably indicate when Nintendo will hold its next presentation\.

Retailer listings sometimes reveal games, editions, or release dates before publishers announce them\. However, they can also contain placeholders, copied product data, and incorrectly matched information\. In this case, the connection to another confirmed August 4 release makes the error explanation particularly convincing\.

**Newly released game**: Palworld 1\.0 Patch Notes: 72 New Pals, World Tree, Sunreach and Major Changes

## Nintendo Has Only Confirmed a 2026 Release

Nintendo officially revealed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time during its June 9 Nintendo Direct\. The company said the Nintendo 64 classic would return for a new generation exclusively on Switch 2 in 2026\.

The brief announcement trailer introduced the project but did not show extended gameplay\. Nintendo also withheld the exact release date, price, editions, and pre-order details\.

The company’s official store page still lists only “Coming 2026\.” It does not currently offer a purchase or pre-order button\.

Nintendo has also avoided explaining the full scope of the project\. The announcement describes Ocarina of Time as “reborn,” but we still do not know how closely it will follow the original game or the enhanced Nintendo 3DS version\.

More information should arrive before launch, particularly details about its updated visuals, controls, gameplay revisions, and technical performance on Switch 2\.

**See also**: Bethesda Finally Reveals What Comes Next for Fallout and The Elder Scrolls VI

## Play-Asia Lists the Game for $59\.99

Although GameStop does not currently accept Ocarina of Time pre-orders, Play-Asia has published product pages for several regional physical editions\.

The retailer lists the game for $59\.99 and marks its expected shipping date as TBA\. Customers can currently add the product to their carts, but Nintendo has not confirmed the price\.

The $59\.99 figure could represent genuine distributor information\. It could also be an estimated or placeholder price that Play-Asia will update later\.

Buyers should therefore avoid treating it as Nintendo’s official US launch price\. Nintendo could use different pricing across physical and digital editions, regions, or special packages\.

The listing does at least support the expectation that Ocarina of Time will receive a physical Switch 2 release\. However, final availability, packaging, and regional language support could change before launch\.

**Related news**: Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake Listed at $59\.99 Ahead of Nintendo Price Confirmation

## When Will Official Pre-Orders Begin?

Nintendo has not announced when pre-orders will open\. Any specific date remains speculation until Nintendo or an authorized retailer publishes confirmed purchase information\.

A new Nintendo Direct or dedicated Zelda presentation would be the most likely place for the company to reveal gameplay, editions, pricing, and a firm release date\. Retail pre-orders could open shortly after that announcement\.

For now, fans should treat the August 4 GameStop date as an apparent listing error rather than a reliable leak\.

The remake itself is official, and Nintendo still plans to release it for Switch 2 in 2026\. The rumored pre-order date is not\.

# Senate's 90-6 CR Freezes Space Force Satellites, Denies War Munitions Authority

Chairman of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Senator Rand Paul \(C\) speaks during a Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs business meeting to consider pending calendar business on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, on August 6, 2026\. The committee is scheduled to vote on whether to hold Dr\. Anthony Fauci, who led the US response to the COVID-19 pandemic, in contempt of Congress\. Brendan SMIALOWSKI/AFP via Getty Images

The Senate voted 90-6 on Saturday to pass a continuing resolution that funds the federal government through December 11, 2026 — averting the threat of a shutdown when FY2027 begins on October 1 — but the bipartisan vote conceals a more consequential outcome for the Pentagon: every dollar of Space Force's $6\.4 billion in requested FY2027 satellite research-and-development increases is frozen at prior-year rates, and five munitions programs actively depleted by the Iran war received no special funding authority at all\.

The bill, developed by Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins \(R-ME\) and Vice Chair Patty Murray \(D-WA\), takes a straightforward approach to the stopgap: fund everything at FY2026 levels, avoid political landmines, and leave the hard choices for when Congress reconvenes in September\. What it does not do is provide any of the Pentagon's requested \"anomalies\" — the special carve-outs that allow specific programs to operate outside the CR's standard freeze\. Neither the $1 billion the White House sought to begin advance nuclear-propulsion procurement for the Trump-class battleship nor the authority to obligate funding on five multiyear munitions contracts made it into either chamber's bill\.

\"This CR is straightforward,\" Collins said in a statement released August 2\. \"It continues current government funding levels until December 11th and includes necessary adjustments for programs like \[WIC\], vital national security programs, including shipbuilding across multiple vessels, and the Disaster Relief Fund\.\" Murray described the Senate version as superior to the House bill because it rejects Trump's war spending requests and closed a loophole that would have allowed the administration to transfer Border Patrol funding from other accounts\.

The ball now sits with the House, which passed its own competing CR — running only through December 4, not December 11 — before departing for recess in July\. The House is scheduled to return August 31, and the Senate is expected to return September 14, leaving roughly 19 legislative days before the September 30 spending deadline to either reconcile the two versions or convince one chamber to adopt the other's bill outright\. If Congress fails, the government would face another shutdown potentially extending through the November midterm elections\.

### Why Does Collins' Cybersecurity Provision Make the Senate Version Different?

One distinction between the two bills that matters specifically to a technology audience: the Senate CR extends two federal cybersecurity authorities that are set to expire September 30, while the House version does not\. Both the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 — which provides privacy and liability protections that allow companies to share data about cyber vulnerabilities with government agencies and each other — and the Federal Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2015 would remain in force through December 11 under the Senate version\. The House CR would let both lapse\. Murray championed this distinction explicitly, describing the Senate bill as one that includes \"important extensions and language that House Republicans' CR did not\.\"

This is a meaningful difference for the House-Senate reconciliation fight ahead\. Democratic support will likely depend on the Senate's cybersecurity extension language surviving, while House Republican leadership has already signaled it prefers the clean, shorter version\. Collins, who faces a competitive re-election bid in Maine, has made bipartisanship on spending a core campaign argument — her track record on this extends to co-sponsoring the Deceptive AI Act with Democrats and Republicans alike, demonstrating her willingness to engage technology policy questions that cross traditional partisan lines\.

### What Does a Continuing Resolution Actually Do to Space Force Programs?

Under standard CR law, the Defense Department is held to its prior fiscal year's appropriations levels and cannot begin new programs, cannot increase spending above those levels in any account, and cannot transfer funds between accounts\. For the Space Force — a service in the middle of the most ambitious satellite modernization push in its history — this is not a paperwork inconvenience\. It is a structural funding gap measured in billions of dollars\.

Space Force's FY2027 budget request asked Congress for $6\.4 billion for satellite programs across three flagship missile warning and tracking satellite programs: the Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared \(Next-Gen OPIR\) constellation, the Resilient Missile Warning and Tracking Medium Earth Orbit \(MEO\) constellation, and the Space Development Agency's Tracking Layer in low Earth orbit \(LEO\)\. Under a CR, none of those increases can be enacted\. Here is what each program receives instead of what it requested:

**Next-Gen OPIR:** FY2026 enacted funding was $1\.4 billion\. FY2027 request: $1\.5 billion\. Under the CR: $1\.4 billion\. Gap: approximately $100 million\. Lockheed Martin is building the geosynchronous-orbit satellites under a contract now valued at a cumulative $8\.2 billion; Northrop Grumman holds the polar constellation contract\. The Space Force has already proposed canceling the polar program in favor of concentrating resources on the LEO and MEO layers\.

**Resilient MWT-MEO:** FY2026 enacted: $675 million\. FY2027 request: $1\.4 billion\. Under the CR: $675 million\. Gap: approximately $725 million — a program the Space Force intended to scale by more than double in a single year is instead frozen at half its intended rate\. Space Systems Command is managing the 30-satellite MEO constellation; the first nine satellites are expected to launch in early 2027\. A CR does not delay launches already under contract, but it does slow the production of subsequent satellite batches and ground system development at a moment when the program's trajectory requires full FY27 funding to stay on schedule\.

**SDA Tracking Layer \(LEO\):** FY2026 enacted: $1\.69 billion\. FY2027 request: $3\.5 billion\. Under the CR: $1\.69 billion\. Gap: approximately $1\.81 billion — the single largest gap across all three programs, and the one with the most immediate operational stakes\. The Space Development Agency's first operational Tranche 1 satellites — built by Northrop Grumman and L3Harris — are expected to launch in 2026\. But as TechTimes has reported, the optical inter-satellite laser mesh that would relay missile warning data across the constellation had not been activated as of July 2026; funding the next tranche of satellite production at $1\.69 billion instead of $3\.5 billion slows a program already running against a compressed timeline\.

All three programs are being realigned under a new Portfolio Executive Office headed by Space Development Agency Director Gurpartap \"GP\" Sandhoo\. The organizational restructuring itself — designed to accelerate integration across the three constellation layers — requires administrative authority and program continuity that a CR does not break, but does not help\.

The National Security Space Launch program, through which the Space Force contracts commercial providers — SpaceX, ULA, and Blue Origin — to carry military and intelligence payloads to orbit, falls in a different category\. Existing NSSL task orders remain funded under the CR; satellites under contract will continue to launch\. However, new competitive contract solicitations for next-phase missions may face scheduling delays if obligation authority for new-year funding cannot be efficiently applied, according to prior Air & Space Forces Magazine reporting on CR impacts on NSSL solicitation timelines\.

### Senate Denies All Five War Munitions Requests — and the Clock Is Running

The munitions picture is starker than the satellite story\. The White House requested authority to obligate funding on five key multiyear munitions programs — the Patriot system's PAC-3 interceptor, the Tomahawk cruise missile, the AMRAAM air-to-air missile, and two Standard Missile-3 variants — arguing that without the carve-out, \"the Government may incur cancellation liabilities on multi-year procurement contracts if it does not order the negotiated production quantities\.\" Neither the Senate nor the House version of the CR includes these authorities\.

The mechanism is specific: under multiyear procurement contracts, the government commits to ordering a defined quantity each year in exchange for reduced per-unit costs — typically 10 to 20 percent below single-year rates\. When a continuing resolution prevents the Defense Department from obligating new-year funds against those agreements, the manufacturer can claim cancellation liability — costs it already incurred to set up production lines, train workers, and purchase materials in anticipation of an order that never arrived\. The Pentagon has been actively using these contracts to ramp up production for all five programs in response to inventory depletion during Operation Epic Fury, the Iran war campaign now in its sixth month\.

The Defense Department's own position, declared in a report published today, is that the 30-year procurement model that governs how it acquires these weapons is broken\. With FY2027 NDAA authorization still blocked in the Senate — and now both chambers operating under competing CR versions — the industry's ability to execute even existing framework agreements for PAC-3, Tomahawk, and AMRAAM production faces another layer of uncertainty\.

The National Taxpayers Union, in pre-vote analysis of the CR, described FY2026 as \"marred by unprecedented brinkmanship over government funding,\" citing a pattern of disruptions that has compounded throughout the year — including a 43-day government-wide shutdown that began when FY2026 opened last October, a 4-day partial shutdown in late January, and a 76-day Department of Homeland Security funding lapse that ran from February through April\. The NTU's broader message: Congress must pass a funding measure before September 30 to prevent a pre-election shutdown\.

### What Reconciliation Money Protects — and What the CR Still Freezes

One important nuance: the $24\.4 billion that Congress allocated toward Golden Dome through last year's reconciliation bill is not frozen by the CR\. Reconciliation funding operates through a different statutory authority and is not subject to the annual appropriations freeze\. The Space Force's contracts with SpaceX for space-based airborne moving target indicator satellites \($4\.16 billion\), communications satellites \($2\.29 billion\), and the NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 ceiling raise to $17 billion — all awarded before the CR period — are similarly unaffected for their existing task orders\.

What the CR does freeze is the baseline discretionary appropriations that fund the Space Force's research, development, and acquisition accounts at the program level\. The three satellite constellations described above draw primarily from these accounts\. The reconciliation money addresses procurement at a macro level; the CR cuts the per-program funding that translates architectural decisions into hardware\. Both pools matter for a program as complex and timeline-sensitive as Golden Dome's space layer\.

### What Comes Next Before October

The House is scheduled to return from recess August 31, and the Senate is expected to return September 14\. The two chambers will need to either reconcile the competing CR versions — the Senate's December 11 end date vs\. the House's December 4 — or convince one chamber to simply adopt the other's bill\. The Senate CR contains several provisions the House version lacks: the two cybersecurity authority extensions, the OMB grantmaking rule block, and various anomalies backed by Democrats that the House's clean version omits\. House Republican leadership is unlikely to accept all of these\.

The deeper problem is what the September calendar already has in it\. Senate Majority Leader Thune filed cloture on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act crypto market-structure bill on August 8 — the same morning he finalized the recess agreement — effectively committing the chamber's first September week to a different fight\. With roughly three usable September weeks before senators depart for midterm campaigning, the legislative runway to a reconciled CR is narrow even before accounting for any renewed attempt to advance the NDAA or a supplemental Iran war funding request\.

\"Fiscal year 2026 has been marred by unprecedented brinkmanship over government funding,\" said the National Taxpayers Union\. \"Congress must enact another funding measure before \[September 30\] to prevent a pre-election shutdown\.\"

For the defense industrial base and the commercial space sector, the CR extends a familiar period of managed uncertainty\. Contractors on active NSSL missions, existing satellite production contracts, and GPS system upgrades can plan with confidence through December 11\. But program offices that were poised to move from planning to procurement in FY2027 — and that depended on the $6\.4 billion in new satellite R&D and the five munitions multiyear authorities — are operating against a FY2026 ceiling that doesn't fit the FY2027 program plan\.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How does the continuing resolution affect my ability to get information about the Space Force's missile warning capabilities?

Directly, it does not — operational missile warning satellites already on orbit continue to function regardless of the CR\. What the CR affects is the funding pipeline for next-generation replacement satellites and the proliferated constellations that Golden Dome's intercept architecture depends on\. The MEO constellation's first nine satellites are expected to launch in early 2027 on a schedule set by prior contracts; a CR delays the production of subsequent batches and the ground systems that would integrate their data\. Readers who follow national security space programs should understand that the bipartisan 90-6 vote does not mean these programs are fully funded — it means they will continue at FY2026 rates until Congress either passes a full appropriation or the December 11 CR expires\.

### What happens to Patriot, Tomahawk, and AMRAAM production without the CR anomaly?

The CR does not stop production outright — weapons manufacturers are currently building these munitions under existing contracts\. What the anomaly denial means is that the Defense Department cannot obligate new-year funding to exercise the negotiated production quantities it committed to under multiyear contracts\. This creates what the White House called a cancellation liability risk: if the government fails to order the agreed quantity, manufacturers can claim costs already incurred for production that the government did not follow through on\. The practical consequence is that production line investments manufacturers made in anticipation of FY2027 orders — workforce training, materials procurement, facility tooling — sit in legal and financial limbo until a full appropriation or a subsequent CR with the anomaly included is enacted\.

### Could the government shut down again on October 1 even with the Senate CR passed?

Yes\. The Senate CR still must be reconciled with the House version — which runs through December 4, not December 11, and lacks the Senate's cybersecurity authority extensions and other provisions — before it can be sent to the president's desk\. Neither bill has been signed into law\. The House is scheduled to return August 31, but the Senate does not return until September 14, compressing the window to fewer than 19 working days before the September 30 deadline\. If no reconciled version passes by then, the government faces another funding lapse\. The September legislative calendar is already crowded: Senate leadership has committed the first September week to a crypto market-structure bill, leaving roughly two weeks to resolve both the CR fight and anything else that surfaces\.

### Why does the Senate CR matter to cybersecurity professionals if it's primarily a defense appropriations story?

The Senate CR extends two federal cybersecurity laws — the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 and the Federal Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2015 — through December 11\. Both are set to expire September 30\. CISA 2015 provides the privacy and liability protections that allow private companies to share threat intelligence about cyber attacks with CISA, the FBI, and each other without legal exposure\. If this extension does not survive the House-Senate reconciliation process, those protections lapse on October 1, potentially chilling the threat-sharing that the federal cybersecurity apparatus depends on during a period when Iran-linked cyber actors have escalated activity targeting U\.S\. critical infrastructure\.
